objective: Make API request failures easier to diagnose and less inconsistent. Today the dashboard's three API client modules each handle failure differently: frontend/src/lib/api.ts throws a typed BackendOfflineError for transport failure and a plain Error for non-2xx, frontend/src/lib/chat-client.ts throws plain Errors with hand-written messages, and frontend/src/lib/workspace-client.ts does the same with yet another message (it tells the developer to run `pnpm dev:app` while api.ts says `pnpm dev:server`). On the server side, backend/server/src/app.ts only logs unexpected errors ('Internal server error' at line 313) and logs nothing at all for 4xx/5xx responses raised by handlers, so a failing request leaves no trace. If nothing changes, every failure a developer or user hits is either silently swallowed or reported with a message that varies by call site.
outcomes: All dashboard API failures go through one typed error that carries the HTTP status and the backend's error message, thrown consistently by frontend/src/lib/api.ts, chat-client.ts and workspace-client.ts
A failure to reach the backend still throws the existing BackendOfflineError from api.ts so app/error.tsx keeps rendering the 'backend did not answer' page
Every non-2xx API response is logged once on the server with method, path, status and message
A non-JSON or empty error body no longer produces a message that is an object or undefined; the thrown message is always a non-empty string

evidence.excerpt: Improve the error handling and logging for API requests.

class BackendOfflineError extends Error { ... } / if (!res.ok) { const body = (await res.json().catch(() => ({}))) as { error?: string }; throw new Error(body.error ?? `The backend answered ${res.status} for ${path}`) }

throw new Error(`Cannot reach the IntentGuard backend at ${API_URL}. Start it with: pnpm dev:server`) vs workspace-client.ts: `... pnpm dev:app` — same situation, two different instructions and two different error types

if (!res.ok) { const data = await res.json().catch(() => ({})); throw new Error(data.error ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`) } — data is untyped, so a JSON error body without an `error` string yields a status-only message

app.onError((err, c) => { if (err instanceof HTTPException) return c.json({ error: err.message }, err.status); console.error('[intentguard-server]', err); return c.json({ error: 'Internal server error' }, 500) }) — HTTPException paths (400/404/409/502...) return without any log line
Production builds hide error messages, so the advice is static — the error page currently tells the user to run `pnpm dev:server`
"test": "pnpm --filter @intentguard/core --filter @intentguard/server --filter @intentguard/mcp-server test" — frontend has no test script and no test runner configured
